It advocates for the adoption of library-style selection policies to prevent arbitrary censorship on networks.

classification.summary: Carl M. Kadie argues that the intellectual freedom principles developed by librarians over a century should be applied to public and academic computer systems. It concludes by urging sysadmins to adopt library standards for network material to protect academic freedom.

notable_claims: University policies typically evolve from no policy to informal, then overly proscriptive, and finally to a balance of rights and responsibilities.
The University of Illinois transitioned from vague 'conduct deemed undesirable' standards to explicitly defined bases for discipline by 1973.
Computing policies at the NCSA in 1991 were viewed as being '20 years behind the times' compared to general university student rights.
classification.summary: Carl M. Kadie analyzes the historical evolution of student policies at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign from 1904 to 1973. He argues that university policies naturally evolve from overly proscriptive regulations toward a balance of rights and responsibilities. The author uses this trajectory to critique contemporary computing policies, specifically those of the NCSA, as being outdated and overly restrictive.
classification.title: From Regulations to Rights: The Maturation of Policy
